overall: The AG found a quorum of the Blandford Selectmen intentionally deliberated outside a posted meeting, failed to follow executive session procedures, and discussed improper topics in executive session; referred for hearing with a recommended $1,000 fine and ordered remedial steps.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two Board members met at Town Hall on Feb 5, 2011 to plan the Feb 7 meeting regarding the Tax Collector, outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: A quorum of the Board (two out of three members) discussed public business within the Board's jurisdiction, outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged Board members' emails deliberated on Tax Collector matters outside a posted meeting, with much discussion of the Feb 7 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Those e-mails constitute deliberations, conducted outside of a properly posted meeting, and therefore violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board entered executive session on Feb 7, 2011 without identifying any statutory purpose in the open session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The Board did not record in the minutes any one of the ten enumerated purposes as its reason for entering executive session, or provide any detail about the reason for the executive session.

allegations.summary: Board did not state before entering executive session whether open session would reconvene afterward, as the law requires.
allegations.key_passage: We assume that the minutes are accurate and thus the required statements were not made.

allegations.summary: Board discussed topics in executive session, including the Tax Collector's management and a Town audit, that were not proper executive session subjects.
allegations.key_passage: This discussion therefore should have occurred in open session, even if the Tax Collector was not available to address the Board's concerns.

remedy: Referred the intentional deliberation violation to a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3) and recommended a $1,000 civil penalty under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
Attend an Open Meeting Law training conducted by an approved attorney or organization, and certify that every Board member attended, within 60 days.
Review and publicly release the portions of the February 7, 2011 executive session minutes where the purpose for executive session has expired, within 60 days.
Publicly release all emails sent or received between and among a quorum of the Board that were provided to this office and are not subject to privilege.
